### 1. Core Problem & Motivation
Ensuring fairness and preventing discrimination in multimodal clinical machine learning tasks, specifically addressing equalized odds on text and tabular data.

*Motivation & Gaps:* Overcoming empirical and methodological bottlenecks in existing approaches to achieve validated outcomes in Exploring Text Specific and Blackbox Fairness.  
*Key Challenges Tackled:*
- Accurate representation and modeling within Exploring Text Specific and Blackbox Fairness
- Empirical validation across benchmarks: MIMIC-III clinical dataset

---

### 2. Proposed Methodology & Technical Architecture
**Architecture Overview:**  
Investigating a modality-agnostic fairness algorithm (equalized odds post-processing) and a text-specific fairness algorithm (debiased clinical word embeddings). The core approach involves ensembling classifiers trained on structured and unstructured data.

**Algorithmic Innovation:**  
Core pipeline execution parameterized across 3 methodological phases.  

*Core Technical Innovations:*
- Problem Formulation & Data Ingestion
- Method Execution & Architecture

### 3. Empirical Results & Benchmark Datasets
**Evaluated Datasets:** MIMIC-III clinical dataset  
**Key Metrics:** Reported Metric, Benchmark Score  

**Quantitative Findings:**  
The dual modality ensemble improves performance and mitigates unfairness relative to constituent components. Equalized odds post-processing diminishes group-specific disparities in TP and TN rates, but this comes with a degradation in AUC. Word embedding debiasing also helps reduce TP/TN discrepancies.  

**Baseline Comparison:**  
Demonstrates measurable findings and comparative evaluation relative to baseline frameworks reported in Exploring Text Specific and Blackbox Fairness.
